subject: SLA pricing: escalation tie-breaker & retainer options
messages:
From: Claire Summers <claire@storix.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: joe.miller@storix.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA & escalation coverage — initial pricing ask

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Storix is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement asked me to get a clear options table for SLA tiers and the associated retainer/escalation pricing so we can budget. A few specific asks: 

- Can you price a 99.9% vs 99.95% uptime tier and show the monthly retainer for 24x7 escalation coverage vs business-hours only?
- We have a quirky failover need: if two of our primary regions experience issues concurrently, we need a "tie-breaker" policy that guarantees routing to a warm standby and an escalation path. How does Redwood price that sort of multi-region tie-breaker support?
- Any step-down discounts for months where usage is <50% of committed throughput?
- Can you attach a sample quote and the SLA wording for uptime credits (we need the exact math for finance).

I attached a one-week export of our usage to give you a sense of peak vs baseline. Goal is a 12–24 month commitment decision next week.

Appreciate quick guidance — Claire

--
Claire Summers
Head of Infrastructure
Storix.ai

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Summers <claire@storix.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA & escalation coverage — initial pricing ask

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the notes and the usage file. Quick summary below and I attached a detailed XLS with pricing breakouts. High-level options: 

Option A (Standard): 99.9% uptime, Business-hours escalation (M-F 8am-6pm PT), $6k/month retainer, 25 on-call hours included, per-incident triage included at no additional cost for incidents within the retainer window.

Option B (Assured): 99.95% uptime, 24x7 escalation, $14k/month retainer, 75 on-call hours included, faster TTR SLA for P0s (2 hours) and a guaranteed warm-standby failover orchestration within 90 minutes when requested.

Tie-breaker multi-region add-on: for concurrent region failures where we perform active warm-standby routing and DR orchestration, we treat that as an "assured incident" and charge a fixed surcharge of $5k per event + hourly incident labor above retainer. If you commit to a 24-month annualized contract we can reduce the event surcharge to $3k.

Step-down discounts: we support a 20% step-down on the retainer for months where committed throughput utilization is <50% for the trailing 30 days (documented by mutual logs). Step-downs are pro-rated and can be invoked up to twice per contract year.

Uptime credit math is in the attached XLS. Short version: credit = (1 - observed_uptime / SLA_target) * monthly_commit, subject to max cap (up to 50% of monthly retainer) and min incident threshold (30 minutes).

Next steps: 
- If the tie-breaker add-on looks like the right risk transfer, I can get legal to send a draft addendum reflecting the event surcharge and standby SLA wording.
- If you'd like preferred pricing, confirm whether you want 12 or 24 month commitment and an expected average QPS.

Attaching: redwood-sla-pricing-quote.xlsx (pricing + SLA excerpt) and I included a small sample mutual action plan at the top of the sheet.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the tradeoffs. Looping Ben and Vanessa for ops/discount approval.

Best,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Claire Summers <claire@storix.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: joe.miller@storix.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA & escalation coverage — initial pricing ask

Grace — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups after reviewing the spreadsheet: 

1) Tie-breaker surcharge: procurement won't accept an open-ended hourly labor bill. Would Redwood consider capping incident labor for tie-breaker events to a fixed not-to-exceed labor fee if we take the 24-month commit?
2) Step-down: good to see the 20% option. Can the two allowed step-down invocations be used consecutively (e.g., two slow months in Q1)?
3) Uptime credit: your formula makes sense, but our finance team needs the exact pro-rata examples for a 30-day month and for leap months to model. Is that in the XLS?

Also — can you share any customer references who have taken the tie-breaker product? We want an ops contact who can talk through a real DR event.

If you can answer these in email we can prep a redline request and aim to sign next Thursday.

Thanks,
Claire

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Claire Summers <claire@storix.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA & escalation coverage — initial pricing ask

Claire — quick answers inline: 

1) Tie-breaker labor cap: Yes — for 24-month commits we can cap labor on a tie-breaker event to $12k not-to-exceed (includes the $3k event surcharge + up to 9 incident hours of labor). We'll add that to the addendum and flag it for legal.

2) Step-downs: consecutive invocations are allowed but limited to two consecutive months; after that, a 30-day re-evaluation period is required before the next step-down. We'll put that language in the contract notes.

3) Uptime credit worked examples: included in the XLS (rows 12–20) with 30-day and 31-day month calculations and an example for 28/29-day months. If procurement wants a one-page appendix with the algebraic formula only, Ben can produce that.

References: I can introduce you to one of our customers who used the tie-breaker add-on last year (we supported a two-region failover for them). I'll confirm permission to share their ops contact and follow up by EOD tomorrow.

Planned next steps: Ben will draft a short addendum with the labor cap + tiered surcharge and Vanessa will confirm operation runbooks for warm-standby orchestration. If you sign within next week we'll apply an early-commit 5% credit to the first 6 months.

Would you like a 30 minute call with Ben + Vanessa tomorrow morning to finalize language?

Cheers,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
